comments.text: Born in Amsterdam, now living in the UK . I live on a hill, but right next door are what is called The Levels. Low lying country which used to be covered in water every winter until in the 900s the Dutch first came here to drain the Levels. They have had to come back, time and time again to repeat the excercise. Why? Because the council refuses to dredge the rhynes, the ditches the Dutch dug out over the centuries, so they could function in keeping the Levels dry. No money, save the voles and other critters that live in or next to the water. All excuses to not spend the money on keeping the land dry and helping the farmers that work there. I'm surprised the Dutch keep coming to help out, the last time after a devastating flood in 2014.
